# DESeq2 Differential Expression & Heatmap Visualization
# Author: Talha Ayub
# Purpose: Analyze RNA-seq counts and generate heatmaps for BGC-Analysis
# Repository: github.com/talhaayub597/BGC-Analysis

# Load required libraries
library(DESeq2)
library(pheatmap)
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Import the counts matrix generated by nf-core (salmon.merged.gene_counts.tsv)
# IMPORTANT: Replace the file path below with your actual path
counts <- read.table("./Results_RNAseq/salmon.merged.gene_counts.tsv",
header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t")

# 2. Filter low-expression genes (keep genes with >10 reads in at least 3 samples)
keep <- rowSums(counts > 10) >= 3
counts_filtered <- counts[keep, ]

# 3. Create DESeq2 dataset
# IMPORTANT: Adjust the 'condition' column based on your actual samples
# Example: c("Rhizome", "Leaf", "Leaf", "Bark", "Leaf")
coldata <- data.frame(row.names = colnames(counts_filtered),
condition = c("Rhizome", "Leaf", "Leaf", "Bark", "Leaf"))

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts_filtered,
colData = coldata,
design = ~ condition)

# 4. Run differential expression analysis
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# 5. Extract normalized counts and plot heatmap of top 50 most variable genes
rld <- rlog(dds, blind = FALSE)
topVarGenes <- head(order(rowVars(assay(rld)), decreasing = TRUE), 50)
mat <- assay(rld)[topVarGenes, ]

# 6. Generate and save Heatmap as PNG
pheatmap(mat,
scale = "row",
main = "Top 50 Variable Genes in Turmeric/Neem/Green Tea",
clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
show_rownames = FALSE,
filename = "Top50_Heatmap.png")

print("Analysis complete! Heatmap saved as 'Top50_Heatmap.png'")
